judgement_1_research_gate_split: The split is the right reading, and the writer refusing too would be wrong. 反例3 as written on the card is about a *shortcut being taken and shown* -- 缺网络跳过复用门自研 -- and the harm is a reader being presented with a completed reuse stage that has no research behind it. That is a display claim, so it belongs at the reader. RecordReuseDecision's own contract is narrower and is fully enforced: the payload conforms, the decision passes the guard, every cited artifact exists and is visible in this project, and the stage row it writes is its own. Refusing to *record* on the absence of a RESEARCH row would invert the ordering the card sets up, because recording the decision is exactly how a project that never ran project.bootstrap gets its evidence into the store at all -- the reader-side gate would then be untestable, and the product-path assertion W0801-PRODUCT-PROJ-REFUSES-WITHOUT-RESEARCH-ROW exists only because a decision was legitimately recorded over a project with no research row.

One consequence the split creates and I want on the record: a store can hold REUSE_DECISION=COMPLETED that no reader will display. That is coherent -- the projection refuses and names the state -- and my R1-M12 run confirms all three reader arms go red when the gate is removed, including the one computed from the real stored row. But it means 'COMPLETED in the database' is not a claim that anything is presentable, and whatever reader is eventually wired must re-derive, not trust. The projection already does re-derive (R1-M14 and R1-M15 both caught), so the discipline is in the code; it should also be stated in W08-99's gate text so a later window does not read the stage table directly. Accept as is.
judgement_2_absent_as_a_value: ABSENT does not cross the 15_NEW_PROJECT_WORKFLOW.md §7 line, and I checked this as a persistence question rather than a naming one. The rule forbids letting internal stage evidence (源码检视、Jev建议、硬门、采用策略、验证) add or replace TaskStatus. Measured: 'ABSENT' occurs exactly twice in the whole of internal/ -- adoption.go:115 (StageProjectionTurn.Status, a returned struct) and adoption.go:183 (the string the refusal message interpolates) -- and appears in no stored row, no constant block, and no file under apps/. The stored stage statuses remain the W05-03 set in project_workspace.go:583-590 (COMPLETED/PARTIAL/FAILED/NOT_STARTED), which this card did not modify, and ProjectStages never writes. So no persisted vocabulary grew by one value.

Substantively, ABSENT is what keeps W05-03's own guarantee alive rather than what breaks it: the comment at adoption.go:8-11 says the NOT_STARTED rows were written deliberately so an absent row cannot be read as 'nothing left to do'. Collapsing the two -- my R1-M11 and R1-M13 mutants, both caught -- is precisely the reading the earlier card guarded against, and the projection cannot tell 'queued and untouched' from 'this project never got a bootstrap row' without a second value. Keeping it as a derived read-side value rather than a writable status is the right compromise. The one thing I would require of whoever wires a reader: do not let ABSENT leak into a client-protocol enum, at which point it would start becoming a status. Today it cannot, because the schema is frozen and no reader exists.
judgement_3_unwired_reader: Not a blocker for this card, and not fully delivered either: a limitation that must travel on the row. I verified the blockage is real rather than asserted -- a whole-repo .go reference search puts every one of the five new exported names inside adoption.go, its three tests and the check program, and `grep -i reuse internal/domain/http.go` returns nothing, so getProjectState has no path to the projection. getProjectState lives in a file whose owning card (W03) is ACCEPTED, and apps/cli and apps/desktop are in nobody's scope here; W08-01's write scope is internal/domain/research*.go, internal/domain/adoption*.go, tests/research/** and its receipts. Demanding the reader now would be demanding an out-of-scope edit, which the card's own 失败与恢复 section forbids ('只改本卡登记范围').

But the honest framing is that card action 1 says init and Desktop must USE the projection, and today they do not use it because nothing reads it. The distinction the executor draws -- shared as a function, and both the record path and the product HTTP path go through it -- is true only of the write path, and the registry note ('drives the production HTTP+SQLite handler for the guard, the projection, the record path and the gate') overstates how far HTTP reaches: the project and the four sealed artifacts do come from the real handler, but the decision itself is submitted by calling s.RecordReuseDecision as a Go method, and there is no route to post it. The receipt's own not_verified_by_design and scope_note do disclose the missing reader, so this is loose wording in one registry note rather than a false report.

I accept with the obligation restated and tightened, and I would convert to a blocker for W08-99 rather than for this card: W08-99 must not sign off 反例3 or J01's 高分硬失败 as user-observable while the only consumer of the projection is a test binary, and must not count the card's deliverable-1 '产品路径' clause closed on this slice's authority. Commit 22eb5bdd already files this and names the owner as W03 or W13 with its own review, which is the right routing; that filing plus this restatement is what should be carried, not a silent pass.
judgement_4_commands_json_precedent: The precedent covers this append, and it covers it far more strongly than the receipt claims. The receipt cites W07-01 and W07-02; measuring `git log -- execution/v2.4/commands.json` I count 23 commits touching it, and the binding cards among them include W02-02, W02-03, W03-01, W03-02, W04-01, W04-02, W05-01, W05-02, W06-01, W06-02, W12-01, W13-01, W13-02, W17-01, W07-01 and W07-02 before this card. No card's write_scope grants execution/v2.4/commands.json -- I read W07-01, W07-02, W04-01 and W03-01 directly to check, and each lists only product, test and receipt paths -- yet every card that binds a selector has edited it. So this is not a two-card exception stretched again; it is how every selector on this line has ever come into existence.

The reason is structural, not habitual: this card's own binding line says 'W02 registers this exact selector and real handler before use; UNBOUND/zero assertions is not PASS', and the dispatcher refuses an unbound key with exit 3. The card therefore cannot be executed as written without a registry entry, and no path inside its declared write scope can create one. A strict reading of write_scope makes the card unsatisfiable, which is a defect in the generated card, not in the executor.

On the shape of the edit, W08-01 is the conservative case: I diffed it against revision 19 and got 21 unchanged pre-existing entries, one added key, one metadata field, and selectors narrowed to W08/W08-01 with owner_card W08-01. W07-02, which was accepted, modified an existing entry in place, which is the stronger act. What should carry forward is not a ruling on this card but a fix at the generator: either add execution/v2.4/commands.json to the write scope of any card that binds a key, or make selector registration a W02-owned step so implementers stop borrowing precedent for an operation the process requires. Until then every future card re-litigates this.
judgement_5_late_landing_guards: The final matrix does cover the late-landing RESEARCH no-skip gate, and it does not cover the probe depth cap -- which is the correct outcome for one and a real gap for the other, and I can name the guards still removable without turning the run red. Measured with my own edits: the gate is caught three independent ways, since removing it (R1-M12) reddens W0801-PROJ-NO-SKIP-WITHOUT-RESEARCH, W0801-PROJ-NO-SKIP-WHEN-RESEARCH-ROW-ABSENT and W0801-PRODUCT-PROJ-REFUSES-WITHOUT-RESEARCH-ROW together; renaming ABSENT to NOT_STARTED in the namer (R1-M13) reddens the ABSENT arm specifically; and admitting RESEARCH=FAILED (R1-M17) is caught by TestW0801ProjectionRefusesAReuseDecisionWithoutResearch in the in-package suite though not by the bound command. So M16 in their matrix is a real mutant of a real gate.

The cap is different in kind, and their matrix has no mutant for it at all: R1-M32 shows it is not falsifiable while the guard stands, and R1-M33 shows its branch is never executed in a clean build. I would not call that a hole in the tests -- it is a safety property of the verification harness, and the right demand is not 'add a mutant' but 'say plainly in the report that the cap is untested by design and why', which the receipt's mid_card_failure_disclosed entry for the storm substantially does.

Guards I can still delete without turning the BOUND command red: the decision-kind enum (R1-M08), the VersionRef entity_type leg (R1-M09), input_revision positivity (R1-M10), the RESEARCH=FAILED arm (R1-M17), the receipt required-key loop (R1-M21) and s.effective on the adoption ref (R1-M28), plus the per-stage reader-action wording (R1-M16c) and commit-error propagation (R1-M30 as originally written). Two of those eight -- the enum and the FAILED arm -- are picked up by the in-package go test, so they are visible on the card but invisible to the bound command, which is itself the finding that matters for VB-2: the registered selector cannot see half of this card's own falsification evidence. The other six survive both oracles; see survivors_explained.

survivors_explained.why_it_survives: The only fixture that exercises this leg, adoption_test.go:96 'adoption ref points nowhere', passes Object{entity_type: Task, id: t} -- which also has no content_hash, so the surviving id/content_hash legs refuse it and the test cannot tell which leg fired. A ref with entity_type Task plus a valid id and content_hash would be accepted.
survivors_explained.severity: minor. Fail-open on a shape the store itself constrains: s.effective and readObject still resolve by project and id, and every real caller builds the ref with domain.Ref(o, 'Artifact'). Fix by giving the test a ref that differs ONLY in entity_type.

survivors_explained.guard: input_revision must be a positive integer
survivors_explained.why_it_survives: Every fixture in both oracles uses float64(1) or float64(3); nothing feeds 0, a negative, or a JSON string, so the whole condition is unasserted beyond the required-key loop that runs first.
survivors_explained.severity: minor. The value is a payload claim about which input revision was considered; a 0 would be recorded, sealed and promoted. Cheap to close with one more case row.

survivors_explained.guard: per-stage reader action wording for NOT_STARTED stages
survivors_explained.why_it_survives: W0801-PROJ-READER-ACTION-EVERY-INCOMPLETE asserts only non-emptiness, so collapsing every NOT_STARTED stage onto the generic 'start this stage' line keeps it green, as does the in-package test which likewise checks != "". R1-M16 shows the emptiness half IS asserted; only the stage-appropriateness half is not.
survivors_explained.severity: cosmetic-to-minor, and it is the weakest of the six. Card action 1 asks that a user see what is owed next, and 'start this stage' is a worse answer than 'run a research cycle over the declared sources', but it is not a false answer.

survivors_explained.guard: ReuseJevGate requires status, selected and signals keys
survivors_explained.why_it_survives: The receipt() helper in the check program and every fixture always set all five keys, so no input ever lacks one. Removing the loop changes nothing observable.
survivors_explained.severity: minor and mitigated. Everything the loop protects is re-derived downstream: a missing status fails the != DECIDED check, a missing selected fails the TrimSpace check, and a missing signals list makes found stay false and returns 'no qualified candidate'. So the loop is a clearer error message over a gate that already refuses, not the gate.

survivors_explained.why_it_survives: The harness always seals a live Artifact and hands back its own Ref, so the effectiveness read never has anything to refuse. Neither oracle feeds a superseded or wrong-project ref.
survivors_explained.severity: the most substantive of the six, because it is the only leg that lets a decision point at an adoption artifact that has been superseded, and this is the compare-and-swap discipline the rest of the line cares about. It is still bounded: the sealed decision bytes are uploaded and sealed inside the same transaction, the ref's content_hash and id are shape-checked, and no product reader consumes the projection yet, so nothing user-facing can show a stale adoption today. Belongs in W08-02's or W08-99's fixture list, not as a rewrite demand here.

survivors_explained.why_it_survives: Structurally: the routing guard at main.go:286 returns before the probe branch at :297, so neutering the cap cannot be observed while the guard stands, and R1-M33 independently shows the cap branch is dead in a clean build. The go-test oracle cannot see main.go at all.
survivors_explained.severity: not a defect. This is verification-harness protection, and its unfalsifiability is expected. Recorded so my survivor list is complete, and the corresponding ask is disclosure, not code.

findings.receipt_accuracy: I looked specifically for false statements in the receipt, since a reporting defect is grounds to reject the report. The material claims all hold under my own measurement: PASS 64 (mine: 64, four runs), byte-identical stdout across four named invocations (mine: same digest, six of their runs plus my own), 17 mutants caught (mine: reproduces all 17 with independent edits), registry rev 20 changing nothing pre-existing (mine: verified by deep diff), 21 pre-existing entries (mine: verified count and identity), test.domain re-measured at 49 (mine: 49), routing refusals at exit 3 for W08-02/W08-99/W09-99 (mine: all three), the accepted evidence set unmoved (mine: 518 entries, zero moved), the VB-2 attribution retracted for the six selector rows (mine: consistent -- those reds are unknown-selector refusals, not toolchain failures), and the two mid-card defects fixed (mine: R1-M35 and the positive control). The mutation attempts ledger (a through h) is candid to a degree I have not seen required, and I checked its shape claim independently: their own first pass did leave four mutants proving nothing, and my M04-equivalent did not need a rewrite because I built the anchor differently. Three things are loose rather than false, and I record them as limitations rather than as grounds to reject: the 'caught: 17' framing implies completeness it does not claim in detail; the registry note overstates HTTP reach for the guard, projection and gate; and the flake classification carries two rows I could not make flip plus one row that is deterministic, not flaky.

limitations: L-1 (carried, must gate W08-99): no init, Desktop or HTTP reader consumes ProjectStages and no route reaches RecordReuseDecision. Card action 1's 'USE' and deliverable 1's '产品路径' are satisfied only at function and store level. Scope-forced, disclosed by the executor, filed by 22eb5bdd with W03/W13 as owner. Reproduction: `grep -i reuse internal/domain/http.go` returns nothing and `grep -rn 'ProjectStages\|RecordReuseDecision' internal/ apps/ tests/` hits only adoption*.go and tests/research/check/main.go. W08-99 must not close the health-and-coverage clause on this slice's authority.

L-2: J01's 热门但不适配 has no assertion of its own; three of the four named refusals do. Reproduction: search the 64-id roster for any id naming popularity-vs-fit; the closest are W0801-JEV-HARDFAIL-OVERRIDES-SCORE and W0801-JEV-NO-QUALIFIED-SIGNAL-REFUSED, which test different claims. Owed at C05, which belongs to W08-99.

L-3: six guards survive both the bound command and the in-package tests: R1-M09 (VersionRef entity_type), R1-M10 (input_revision positivity), R1-M16c (per-stage reader-action wording), R1-M21 (receipt required-key loop), R1-M28 (s.effective on the adoption ref), R1-M32 (probe depth cap, expected). The first five are one fixture row each away from being falsifiable; R1-M28 is the one I would rank as a real hole. None is a card-named guard or one of the three counter-examples.

L-4: two further guards are covered ONLY by `go test ./internal/domain` and are invisible to the registered selector -- R1-M08 (decision-kind enum) and R1-M17 (the RESEARCH=FAILED arm of the no-skip gate). No Go key in execution/v2.4/commands.json runs that suite, so obligation VB-2 leaves a third of this card's own falsification evidence unreachable from any bound command. This is a line-level gap, not a W08-01 defect, and it should be fixed by whoever owns the registry rather than by this card.

L-5: TestW17UpgradeActiveRecovery is deterministically red at HEAD (3/3, no such table: runtime_dispatches, backup_upgrade_test.go:699), pre-existing and not this card's doing; and I could not reproduce the pass<->flip intermittency the receipt attributes to TestIntentQualifiedNativePlannerToBusinessDAG / TestRuntimeCoordinatorPeriodicHeartbeat, which passed 3/3 for me. The attribution to W08-01 being innocent is right; the 'intermittent' label is one I will not repeat from my own evidence, and the loopback-proxy mechanism should be recorded on the checkpoint rather than resting in a receipt footnote. Reproduction: the go test command in methods[].

No registered evidence path pins checkpoint.json, commands.json or step_state.json, so no frozen evidence moved. Should be corrected on the next checkpoint write, and is not a reason to withhold acceptance.

L-7: coverage I did not measure. I re-ran three of the ten accepted-selector rows (test.domain 49, test.context 282, test.security 148, all matching) and did not re-run contracts.validate, test.orchestration, test.resources, test.runtime, test.sources.live, test.ui.routes or test.ui.recovery; their PASS rows are taken from the receipt, and I verified only that the registry append changed no pre-existing entry, which is the structural reason those rows cannot have moved. I did not re-run the in-package tests of other cards beyond the three named above, did not execute R1-M34, and did not verify the plan_sha256 or spec_manifest_sha256 values in the receipt against the package's own manifest (no manifest.json at the package root, and I did not recompute the spec-manifest hash).

L-8: internal/domain/research*.go is inside write scope and the card created no file there, so B01/B02 as possibly-research-side deliverables were not touched at all; I did not test whether the card text's G01-G07 binding in action 2 was intended to be satisfied by the guard's licence/revision/evidence citations, and no roster id names G01-G07.
verdict_scope: ACCEPT_WITH_LIMITATIONS for exactly one check: test.research.fixture as bound for task_id W08 / check_id W08-01 at registry revision 20, measured on tree 2227afd6 (equal to ed8436be for this card's files) with HEAD ed8436be. The verdict covers the four delivered units and the handler behind the bound command; it is not an acceptance of parent W08, of W08-99, of the W08 parent gate, or of formal cases C05 and C06, and it registers no case-level claim.

Nothing in this review rejects the implementation and nothing in it asks for a rewrite. The three limitations I would press are reporting-coverage and ownership matters -- the unwired reader (L-1), the missing 热门但不适配 arm (L-2) and the six unasserted legs (L-3) -- and each is a fixture row, a test case or a routed obligation away, not a wrong behaviour in adoption.go. Where a reporting defect and an implementation defect could be confused, I have assigned the smaller consequence: the loose registry wording about HTTP reach, the 'caught: 17' framing, the 'intermittent' label and the stale dirty_paths field are named as corrections to text, and the code was let stand on measurements of my own. If any future round treats this slice's acceptance as evidence for W08-99's 反例 or J01 sign-off, that is outside what is granted here.

Registration is left to whoever applies this verdict: the row is unsigned and should gain verifier_id = qoder-desktop:/root/w0801_verifier_r1 with limitations L-1 through L-4 carried onto the row text so they survive into the parent gate rather than dying in this file.
